trust_decision.summary: Trusted: the published fix appends `; sandbox allow-scripts` to the Content-Security-Policy of the two /nbconvert handlers (on by default, opt-out via a new ServerApp.nbconvert_csp_sandbox trait plumbed into the web-app settings), confining nbconvert-rendered JavaScript to a unique origin so it cannot reach the Jupyter server.

landing_point.why: The summary names NbconvertFileHandler/NbconvertPostHandler and 'missing sandbox CSP', so an engineer reads those two classes and the moment the exporter output is written to the response (jupyter_server/nbconvert/handlers.py:164-167, :204-207), where the CSP property belongs.

fix_sites.entry_point: ServerWebApplication.init_settings — the settings dict every handler reads (merged with user overrides at jupyter_server/serverapp.py:476-477)
ServerApp.nbconvert_csp_sandbox config trait (config file / serverapp config), inserted after the quit_button trait at jupyter_server/serverapp.py:1601-1605
fix_sites.module_kind: config defaults (traitlets trait on the server application)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver reads the handlers' own `self.settings.get("nbconvert_csp_sandbox", True)` fallback as sufficient and never opens serverapp.py, arguing the trait plus settings key are optional plumbing that does not change the default behaviour.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The CSP property the fix extends is shared: a user-supplied Content-Security-Policy in settings['headers'] must be returned verbatim, and API responses must keep exactly "frame-ancestors 'self'; report-uri <base>/api/security/csp-report; default-src 'none'". Appending sandbox in the base class (jupyter_server/base/handlers.py:93) would also sandbox the JupyterLab app shell served by MainHandler (jupyter_server/base/handlers.py:1104-1111) and the exact-match assertions in tests/services/kernels/test_api.py:99-102.

O6_input_shapes: notebook identified by path and loaded through the ContentsManager (GET /nbconvert/<format>/<path>, jupyter_server/nbconvert/handlers.py:114-129)
notebook supplied inline as a JSON model in the request body, no contents lookup (POST /nbconvert/<format>, jupyter_server/nbconvert/handlers.py:182-185)
any exporter format, not just html — the header is attached to the handler class, so latex/pdf/script/zip responses get it too (jupyter_server/nbconvert/handlers.py:154-167, :200-207)
configuration shape: sandbox on by default, removed when ServerApp.nbconvert_csp_sandbox is False (fix.diff:44-46, fix.diff:82-89)

O7_producer.where: jupyter_server/serverapp.py:1606 produces the trait value and jupyter_server/serverapp.py:459 copies it into application settings; the handler's CSP check reads it from self.settings but never calls either

O8_uncovered_routes.route: KernelSpecResourceHandler serves any file from a kernelspec resource directory with a MIME type guessed from the path (mimetypes.guess_type at :42) and finishes it directly (:44), inheriting the un-sandboxed base CSP, so an .html/.svg kernelspec resource is served in the server origin with no `sandbox` directive
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: kernelspec resources are installed by the operator on disk, not authored as notebook content, and the advisory names only the nbconvert handlers — no nbconvert rendering happens on this route
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another package: jupyter_server/kernelspecs vs jupyter_server/nbconvert, reached via a different default service (jupyter_server/serverapp.py:193-196, :933)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a POST /api/nbconvert/<format> export endpoint on the API twin of the UI route, finishing the exporter HTML directly
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the module already exists in the same 'nbconvert' auth resource and the frontend already calls /api/nbconvert to list exporters (jupyter_server/serverapp.py:197-200), so an API-driven export is a one-handler addition a maintainer would plausibly write without the class-level CSP property

O8b_injection_room.sibling: server-side rendering of the notebook to HTML served straight from ViewHandler instead of the sandboxed iframe preview
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the /view route already exists for previewing files and its only confinement today is the iframe attribute in jupyter_server/templates/view.html:31; a maintainer replacing the iframe with rendered HTML would drop that confinement silently

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a module-level export-and-finish helper (like respond_zip) reused by a lightweight handler that subclasses tornado's RequestHandler rather than JupyterHandler
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: respond_zip and get_exporter are already module-level helpers taking a handler, so a new writer built the same way would never inherit AuthenticatedHandler.content_security_policy and would emit no CSP at all

O9_family: CWE-1021 (improper restriction of rendered UI layers) / CWE-79 (stored XSS) — missing `sandbox` CSP directive on server-rendered HTML

O10_build.toolchain: hatchling build backend, pip/hatch install, pytest with pytest-jupyter[server]>=0.7 and pytest-timeout (pyproject.toml:2-3, :61-64)
services: none external: the jupyter_server app is started in-process by the jp_fetch/jp_serverapp fixtures; nbconvert>=6.4.4 (pyproject.toml:32) and tornado>=6.2.0 (pyproject.toml:44) are ordinary runtime dependencies
O10_build.project_tests: tests/nbconvert/test_handlers.py:1-193 covers both /nbconvert routes (GET file, POST body, sanitize_html, zip) at the pinned commit; CSP behaviour is covered by tests/base/test_handlers.py:29-44 and tests/services/kernels/test_api.py:98-120; no CSP test exists for the nbconvert handlers at the pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: copy AuthenticatedFileHandler's unconditional `+ "; sandbox allow-scripts"` into the two nbconvert handlers (or, worse, into the shared base CSP property), getting the header right but dropping the config opt-out — and in the base-class variant sandboxing the JupyterLab app shell and breaking the exact-match CSP tests

out_of_scope_notes: jupyter_server/base/handlers.py:983 FileFindHandler (/static/) and jupyter_server/base/handlers.py:1184 PublicStaticFileHandler (/robots.txt, /favicon.ico) serve app assets and fixed names with no CSP at all — outside this advisory's protection, noted only.
unverified: Repository size in MB could not be measured (no shell in this session), so tiny_repo/giant_repo are not claimed.
present_in_latest for the O8 route is unknown: no latest tree or release is available in the inputs ('Latest release, for O8 only: none').

The O8 kernelspec route is a same-class CSP-sandbox gap on a different sink (kernel-spec resource files) rather than nbconvert-rendered HTML; whether the advisory's property is read as covering it is a judgement call.

Whether the hidden tests will exercise ServerApp.nbconvert_csp_sandbox=False — the only behaviour that forces the two serverapp.py sites — is unknown; with the handlers' `.get(..., True)` fallback, a solver can omit serverapp.py and still pass every default-path test.
